title: Automated cohort-driven perturbation scans and dynamic bitwidth guardrails
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build an automated evaluation pipeline that runs cohort-specific perturbation scans for candidate quantization profiles (int8/int4, AWQ and GPTQ variants), computes weighted quality deltas across input archetypes and routing cohorts, and produces a dynamic safety-latch signal that can automatically downgrade to a safer bitwidth or route traffic to a higher-fidelity variant when the computed risk exceeds per-cohort budgets. The system must simulate realistic runtime conditions (KV cache warm states, variable sequence lengths, and batching) and surface interpretable attributions (layerwise, token-position, prompt-template) to guide quant profile tuning and model onboarding decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs end-to-end on nightly schedule for all production routes and creates per-cohort quality delta reports
Safety-latch signal is computed and persisted; a smoke test can flip routing to fallback variant given that signal
Attribution artifacts (layerwise heatmaps, high-impact prompt examples) are generated in human-readable reports
False-positive rate of automated safety-latch <= 5% on historical rollout simulations
Documentation and runbook published with troubleshooting steps and escalation path
tasks: Design cohort taxonomy (routes, user cohorts, prompt templates, length buckets)
Extend eval harness to simulate KV cache warm/cold states and batching profiles
Implement perturbation scan runner that applies AWQ/GPTQ profiles and captures logits + tokens
Compute composite quality score (semantic + logit-space + hallucination heuristics) and per-cohort weighting
Design and implement dynamic safety-latch algorithm with hysteresis and cooldown windows
Instrument dashboards: per-cohort delta, top failing prompts, layerwise impact heatmaps
Integrate with rollout service to expose latch signal as a route-level policy
Write runbook, SRE playbook for manual overrides, and QA checklist
metrics: Primary quality delta: cohort-weighted semantic delta (BERTScore or embed-sim) as percent change
Logit divergence: average JS divergence across top-k logits
Hallucination proxy: fraction of responses failing factuality heuristics
Latency change: p95 token latency delta under simulated batching
Safety-latch FP rate on historical sync: percent
Number of auto-rollbacks triggered per week in staging
risks: Over-sensitive latch could cause unnecessary rollbacks, increasing cost and hurting availability
Under-specified cohorts miss important user archetypes leading to missed regressions
Synthetic stress prompts might not reflect real-world failure modes for certain verticals
Comparing AWQ vs GPTQ requires normalized calibration to avoid tooling bias
Runtime simulation complexity (cache/batch) may increase test flakiness and run time
